markdownBody:
## Overview

Classgrid AI is like an extra helper for your email and your week. You type what you need in plain words, and the agent does the work. It can read, write, plan and send things for you. You don't need to learn any new software to use it.

Connect your Gmail or Outlook, and the agent can read your inbox for you. Ask it which emails need a reply today, and it gives you a short list. It can write a reply and send it from your own account when you say so. It can also read the files attached to an email.

Connect Google Calendar and ask what your week looks like. The agent lists your meetings and tells you when you are free. It can add a new meeting, with a Google Meet link if you want one. It can also make Zoom or Outlook meetings. It can't move or cancel a meeting yet, so you still do that yourself.

Need a proposal, a quote or a short report? Tell the agent what it is about, and it writes it and turns it into a clean PDF. It can then email that PDF from your Gmail, with the file attached. You can read it first and ask for changes before anything is sent.

After a meeting, paste your rough notes or upload a voice note. The agent turns them into clear notes with action items and a name next to each one. It can save them as a Notion page or post them in a Slack channel. Everyone sees the same notes without anyone typing them again.

You don't have to sit and watch. Email the task to agent@classgrid.in from the email you signed up with, or call the agent on WhatsApp. It keeps working in the background for up to 48 hours. If it needs something, it asks you on WhatsApp, and it sends you the result when it's done.

Want a nudge at a set time? A schedule can send you a reminder you write, by email or WhatsApp. It sends the same words you set, once or on the days you pick. It does not write a fresh summary each time.

Your team chat can live in a Grids group, with quick polls for decisions. The agent can catch you up on what your group said in the last couple of hours. It always shows you a draft and asks before it posts anything to the group. For bigger work, up to 4 people can share one AI chat and build the answer together.

Each person signs up with their own email. You can connect or disconnect apps at any time from Plugins. You can delete any chat whenever you want. It is free to start, and you top up only when you need more.

## Things to try

Type any of these in Classgrid AI:

- Read my unread emails from today
- What's on my calendar for tomorrow?
- When am I free next week?
- Search my Notion for recent strategy docs
- Write meeting notes and action items.
- Draft a project proposal.
- Create a PDF report in minutes.
- Get reminders on WhatsApp.

| Google Drive | Find and read files, save new ones |
| Slack | Read and post messages, create canvases |
| Notion | Search, create and update pages |

markdownBody:
## Overview

Classgrid AI helps you find facts and make sense of data. You ask a question in plain words. The agent searches, reads and works things out for you. Then it gives you an answer you can check.

When you ask a research question, the agent searches the web and opens the pages it finds. It reads them, even long ones, in parts so nothing important is missed. Then it writes an answer with numbered sources. Click any number to see the page it came from.

The sources are real pages the agent opened. Still, always click through and check the facts that matter most. It does not search paid journal databases. There is no special mode to turn on, you just ask your question.

You can upload PDFs, Word files, slides, Excel sheets, CSV files, images and audio. Up to 6 files fit in one message. Ask questions about them, compare two papers, or pull out tables and quotes. Your files stay in your Library, where you can search for them later.

For numbers, the agent writes real Python code and runs it in a safe sandbox. It can clean messy data, remove repeated rows, fix dates and work out statistics. It shows you each step it took. You get the files back, like a clean Excel sheet.

Ask for a chart and the agent draws one from your data, like a bar, line or pie chart. It can also draw a simple flow diagram. When you're done, ask for a PDF report with your charts and findings. You can download it or share it.

Some answers come as live cards. Ask about a stock and you get its price and a small chart. Ask about the weather and you get today plus the next 5 days. You can also get a map pin, a route or a countdown to a deadline. The market card only shows data and is not financial advice.

Connect Google Drive to find and read your files and save results there. Connect Google Forms to read survey answers, or make a new form. You can also save findings to Notion, read email attachments in Gmail, or run SQL on your Supabase database. Not sure how to write SQL? Ask in plain English and the agent writes it for you.

Want to keep a chat private? Use Incognito, and that chat is not saved to your history. Want to share your findings? Send a read-only link, or share them in a Grids group. It is free to start, and you top up only when you need more.

## Things to try

Type any of these in Classgrid AI:

- Research a topic with real sources.
- Search the web with sources.
- Outline a literature review.
- Analyse a file in seconds.
- Clean up messy spreadsheet data.
- Draw a chart from your data.
- Create a PDF report in minutes.
- Write SQL queries from plain English.

## Overview

Grids is the messaging part of Classgrid AI. You find it as "Grids" in the side menu of the app. It works a lot like the chat apps you already know: you can talk one-to-one with anyone who has a Classgrid AI account, or make groups with many people. The big difference is that your own AI agent lives right next to your chats and can help you with them.

You can start a chat with any person on Classgrid AI by searching their name and pressing "Start Chat". You can also make a group and give it a name and a short subject. A group can be a general group, a team, a department, or an official announcement group. You decide who can see it and join it: it can be private and invite-only, visible but people must ask to join, or open so anyone can join straight away. People can also explore open groups and send requests to join.

Group owners have real control. You choose who can send messages, who can change the group name and picture, who can add new members and who can send files. If you set "Only Admins" for messages, your group becomes a clean notice board where only you post and everyone else reads. You can make other people admins too. Every change in the group is recorded in an audit log, and you can download that log as a sheet.

Messages can do much more than text. You can send voice notes, photos, videos, documents and GIFs. You can mention one person or everyone in the group, react to messages, reply to a message, forward it, pin important ones for a day, a week or a month, and star messages to find them later. You can search inside a chat. You can mark a message as high priority or urgent so it stands out, set it to delete itself at a certain time, or schedule it to be sent later. You can also turn on disappearing messages for chats you do not want to keep.

You always know what is happening. You can see who is online, who is typing or recording, and for every message you can see who has received it and who has read it. New messages pop up even when you are on another page, and you get a badge with the number of unread messages.

You can make polls. Ask a question, add between two and ten options, and choose if people can pick more than one answer. Everyone votes in the group and you can see the results live. This is perfect for picking a day for a meeting, a place for a trip or an idea for a project.

Your AI agent can help with your groups. You can ask it to catch you up on what a group talked about recently, list the members, check a poll's results, write a message or an announcement, make a new poll, or send a file to the group. The agent always shows you its draft first and asks "Should I send this to the group?", and it only sends after you say yes. It looks at groups by default and asks before it reads your private one-to-one chats.

You can share one AI chat with friends using Share Grid. Open any chat with the agent, press the share button, and invite up to three other people by email, from your Grids contacts or with an invite link you can send on WhatsApp. Then all four of you can read the chat, send messages and ask the AI together. Each message shows who sent it, and the agent knows who asked what. It answers one person at a time, so nothing gets mixed up. If the owner leaves, the chat passes to the next person.

You can also share a finished chat as a link. This makes a read-only copy of the chat that anyone can open, and you can post it straight to WhatsApp or LinkedIn or copy the link. Great for showing a good answer, a plan or a piece of research to people who do not use Classgrid yet.

In short: Grids lets you chat, run groups, take votes and post notices, with your AI agent helping you catch up and write, but only posting when you say yes. And with Share Grid, up to four people can work with the same AI chat together.

## Things to try

Type any of these in Classgrid AI:

- Read my Grid
- Catch me up on the team group
- Make a poll: Which day for the launch call?
- Make a poll in the trip group: Goa, Manali or Ooty?
- Who voted in the poll?
- Draft an announcement for the Product launch group about Friday's demo
- Send the launch plan PDF to the Product launch group
- Who is in the Trip plan group?

## Overview

Project Mode is the coding side of Classgrid AI. You switch from "Agent" to "Project" in the app, and you get a full code editor right inside your browser, with an AI agent sitting next to it. It is VS Code, one of the most used code editors, so you do not need to install anything on your computer. You open a tab and start building websites and apps.

To use it you connect your GitHub account, because your code is kept on GitHub, with only a temporary copy while you work. You install the small Classgrid app on the GitHub repos you want to work on, and then you can open any of your projects in one click. If you do not have a project yet, you can start an empty one and ask the agent to build something from nothing, like a website or a small app. When you are ready, the agent can even create a new GitHub repo for you and save the work there.

The editor has everything you expect. There is a file list, a code area, a terminal where you can type commands, a Run button, auto-save, and tools that tidy your code and point out mistakes. When you open a project, it installs the project's packages by itself in the background, so you can start working straight away. Python and Node.js / TypeScript work out of the box.

The agent can really work on your code, not just give advice. You can ask it to fix a bug, add a feature, explain how something works, or build a new page. It reads your files, searches through the code, makes the changes, runs your build or tests, and checks for errors after every change. For big questions, like "how does login work in this project?", it can send up to five small helpers to read different parts of the code at the same time, so you get an answer much faster.

It understands what you are looking at. It knows which file you have open, which lines you have selected and which red error lines the editor is showing. So you can simply select a piece of code and ask "why is this not working?" If your project has a rules file for AI tools, the agent reads it and follows your rules. For bigger jobs it can write a plan first, show it to you, and only start building after you approve it.

You are always in control of every change. After each answer you see a small box that says how many files changed and how many lines were added or removed. You can open "Review" to see every change file by file, in colour, and reject the parts you do not want. Or you can press "Undo" and the whole project goes back to exactly how it was before that answer.

Nothing ever goes straight into your main code. When you save your work, by pressing "Push to GitHub" or by asking the agent, it goes to a new branch and opens a pull request on GitHub. You or the repo owner look at it and decide to merge it. The work is signed by Classgrid AI with you as co-author, so your name is on it too. If someone else changed the same branch in the meantime, it joins their work with yours carefully, and if the same lines clash it stops instead of overwriting anything. If you close the editor and forget to save, your unsaved work is backed up to a separate branch on GitHub, so nothing is lost.

You can put your work online through Vercel. If you connect your Vercel account, the agent can create the Vercel project, add the secret settings your app needs, and deploy your branch as a preview link or as the live site, all on your own Vercel account. Your project cards in Classgrid then show the live address next to the project.

Your projects stay organised. Each project has its own card with a logo, the last change, the branch and the time, plus its own chats, so you can keep one project per client or per idea. You can also move a normal chat into a project if a conversation turns into real coding work.

In short: Project Mode is a full code editor in your browser with an AI that edits, runs and fixes your code, while you stay in charge. Every change can be reviewed or undone, everything is saved safely as a pull request on your GitHub, and you can ship it to your own Vercel when it is ready.

markdownBody:
## Overview

With Classgrid AI you can give work to your AI agent just by talking to it on a WhatsApp call. You do not need to open the app or type anything. You call the Classgrid number, +91 81492 77038, on WhatsApp, say what you need in your own words, hang up, and the agent does the work and sends you the result on WhatsApp. It is like calling a smart assistant who then goes away and gets the job done for you.

Getting ready takes a minute and you only do it once. You sign up on chat.classgrid.in with your email, then verify your WhatsApp number in the app with a six-digit code that arrives on WhatsApp. After that, your number is linked to your account and the AI knows it is you whenever you call.

When you call, the AI picks up and greets you by your first name: "Hi, this is Classgrid AI. What can I do for you?" You talk normally, like on any phone call. You can interrupt it at any time and it will stop and listen. It speaks in English. Each call can last up to fifteen minutes, which is plenty of time to explain a few jobs.

While you are on the call, the AI can answer you live. It can look things up, check your connected apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Notion or GitHub, and tell you the answer right there on the call. If the answer takes a bit longer to find, it does not keep you waiting, it simply sends the answer to you on WhatsApp a little later.

For bigger jobs, the AI notes down what you asked and starts working as soon as you hang up. It sends you "Got it" on WhatsApp so you know it has your request. Then your agent does the work in the background, with all its normal powers: searching the web, writing emails, making reports and PDFs, building or fixing a website, and using your connected apps. Coding jobs go into Project Mode by themselves. When it is done, you get the result on WhatsApp with a link to the full chat, and files like PDFs arrive as real files you can open straight away.

You can add more after you hang up. If you forgot something, just send a WhatsApp message, a photo or a document while the job is still running, and the agent will use it. You can also email extra files to agent@classgrid.in. The agent can keep working on a job for up to two days, waiting for your replies when it needs them.

This is useful in many everyday moments. You can call while driving and ask it to email a client that the quote is approved. You can call in the morning to hear what is on your calendar today. You can describe a report out loud, hang up, and get the finished PDF on WhatsApp. You can ask it to find last week's invoice in your Drive. You can even ask it to fix the contact form on your website while you are away from your laptop.

It is safe and personal. Only a verified WhatsApp number that belongs to one Classgrid account can use the calls, so nobody else can talk to your agent. If an unknown number calls, it gets a message explaining how to sign up and verify first. There is a fair daily limit on calls for each number, and calls use your normal Classgrid AI credits.

A few things to know. It is a WhatsApp voice call, so a normal phone call to the number will not reach the AI. It speaks in English. A WhatsApp text on its own does not start a new job; you start a job by calling or by emailing agent@classgrid.in, and then your messages are added to that job.

How it compares, as of October 2026: most big AI assistants cannot be called on WhatsApp in India today. Grok Bot can make calls to other people for you, but you cannot call it. OpenAI's Dots works inside ChatGPT, Slack and Teams, not on WhatsApp or calls. Meta's Muse is only in the US. Classgrid AI lets you call it on WhatsApp in India, and it does real work after the call and sends the results back to you.

In short: call +91 81492 77038 on WhatsApp, say what you need, hang up, and your Classgrid AI agent gets it done and sends you the result on WhatsApp.

## Overview

Classgrid AI can keep working for you when you are not looking. You can set reminders that come at the right time, and you can give the agent long jobs that keep going after you close the tab. You set it all up by typing in normal words at chat.classgrid.in. It is free to start, and you top up only when you need more.

You can ask it to remind you about anything. It can be one time, every day, every week or only on the days you pick, for up to 90 days. At that time the reminder comes to your email. After you verify your WhatsApp number with a code, it comes on WhatsApp too.

There is one thing to know about reminders. The words are written when you set the reminder up, and the AI does not run again when it is sent. So it is perfect for "call the client at 4" or "drink water and plan tomorrow". It is not for fresh news or a new summary every morning. For a fresh answer, just ask the agent in the chat.

Reminders go only to you, by email and WhatsApp. They can't message other people. You can see all your reminders on the Schedule page in the app.

The agent can also work on long jobs in the background. Give it a big task, like comparing a few products, making a long report or building a list from the web, and close the tab. It keeps going for up to 48 hours. If it needs to wait for a later time or for your answer, it pauses and wakes up again to carry on.

If the agent needs something from you, it can ask you on WhatsApp and wait for your reply. You answer in WhatsApp like a normal message, and it picks up where it left off. When the job is done, you get "Task completed" with a link to the full chat.

Results can come straight to your WhatsApp. If the agent makes a PDF, it sends it as a real file you can open, save and forward. You also get the link to the chat, so you can see everything it did and ask for changes.

You can hand off work without opening the app. Send an email to agent@classgrid.in from the email you signed up with, and the agent starts the task. You can also start a task with a WhatsApp call to +91 81492 77038, say what you need and hang up. Plain WhatsApp texts don't start a new task, but while a task is open you can send extra texts or files to add to it.

In short: set a reminder once and get it on time, or give the agent a long job and walk away. It keeps working, asks you when it needs to, and sends the result to your WhatsApp or email when it is done.

children.text: The Scale Problem Has Become an Infrastructure Problem

As of May 31, 2026, India's higher-education challenge is not merely that more students need access to college. It is that institutions must coordinate learning, attendance, fees, examinations, admissions, compliance, parent communication, student support, and placement preparation at a level of volume and speed that legacy administration was never designed to carry. According to the Ministry of Education's
All India Survey on Higher Education 2021-22

, total higher-education enrolment rose to nearly 4.33 crore, while the system included 1,168 university-level institutions, 45,473 colleges, and 12,002 standalone institutions. The same release reported 1.07 crore pass-outs in 2021-22. At that scale, the unit of reform is no longer the classroom alone; it is the institutional workflow that determines whether a student is visible, supported, assessed, and guided before it is too late.

body.caption: Digital maturity in higher education is moving from paper and spreadsheets toward unified institutional infrastructure.

children.text: For many colleges, the practical reality is still a patchwork: one team manages admissions, another manages fees, faculty track attendance separately, departments circulate notices through messaging groups, and placement preparation often begins late because student performance data is scattered. This does not mean administrators are careless. It means the operating model asks human teams to reconcile too many moving parts without a shared source of truth. The result is delay, duplication, weak visibility, and poor continuity between academic progress and employability preparation.
The Placement Crisis Is a Signal Failure
The employability crisis is often discussed as a student problem, but it is also an institutional intelligence problem. The
India Skills Report 2026

, prepared by ETS with CII, AICTE, AIU, and Taggd, placed India's overall employability at 56.35 percent. Engineering looked stronger than the national average, with B.E./B.Tech employability reported at 70.15 percent, but the headline still conceals a deeper issue: employers are no longer hiring degrees alone; they are hiring evidence of applied capability, communication, adaptability, and technical currency.
Older but still widely cited evidence shows why the problem became so persistent. The SHL/Aspiring Minds
National Employability Report Engineers 2019
found that a large share of Indian engineers were not ready for knowledge-economy roles and that only a small fraction possessed industry-ready AI skills. In 2026, Azim Premji University's
State of Working India 2026

sharpened the warning from the labour-market side: the transition from education to employment remains difficult even as higher education expands, and young graduate unemployment remains a structural concern. These reports differ in methodology, but they point in the same direction: the gap is not just between syllabus and industry; it is between institutional visibility and student readiness.

children.text: AI Has Changed What Prepared Means
AI has compressed the distance between classroom learning and workplace expectation. The Microsoft and LinkedIn
2024 Work Trend Index

reported that 75 percent of global knowledge workers were already using AI at work, while 66 percent of leaders said they would not hire someone without AI skills. GitHub's controlled study on Copilot found that developers using the tool completed a programming task
55 percent faster
than those who did not. The World Economic Forum's
Future of Jobs Report 2025
added that nearly 40 percent of skills required on the job are expected to change by 2030, with the skills gap already cited by 63 percent of employers as a major barrier to transformation.

For education, this does not mean every institution must become a software company. It means rote learning, isolated coding assignments, and end-of-term marks are no longer enough evidence of readiness. Students need project work, problem-solving, AI literacy, communication practice, and feedback loops that help them understand where they stand before placement season. Faculty need tools that surface learning gaps early. Administrators need dashboards that translate academic activity into readiness signals. UNESCO's
guidance on generative AI in education and research
is useful here because it frames AI adoption as a human-centred governance challenge, not a race to automate everything.

children.text: The ERP/LMS Gap Is More Than a Software Gap
Indian institutions have already begun investing in digital transformation, but adoption is uneven. VMware's India-focused
Future of Education Survey

reported that 71 percent of surveyed higher-education institutions were looking to invest in digital workspaces or remote capabilities, and 84 percent had an institution-wide strategic plan for digital adoption, while only 68 percent had allocated budget to support it. Academic research on
digital competence in Indian higher education
also shows that online learning and LMS use expanded during the pandemic, but issues such as device dependence, socio-economic access, and digital capability continued to shape participation.

The deeper issue is that many products digitize one department without redesigning the institution. A fee tool may not understand attendance. An LMS may not connect to admissions. A messaging group may reach students but leave no auditable institutional memory. A spreadsheet may solve one clerk's immediate problem while creating a blind spot for the principal, HOD, or placement coordinator. This is why existing ERPs often fail in the Indian context: they can be expensive, complex, slow to configure, and too removed from the lived workflows of colleges that need affordability, local compliance, multilingual communication, mobile access, and rapid adoption.
NEP 2020 Points Toward Interoperable Digital Infrastructure

The National Education Policy 2020 anticipated this shift. It states that technology will play an important role in improving educational processes and outcomes and calls for the National Educational Technology Forum to support technology use in learning, assessment, planning, administration, and related education functions. In its chapter on online and digital education, NEP 2020 specifically argues for
open, interoperable, evolvable public digital infrastructure
that can work across multiple platforms and point solutions while solving for India's scale, diversity, complexity, and device penetration.

That sentence matters because it moves the conversation beyond buying software. The future institution needs a connected layer where student data, academic data, financial data, attendance records, communication history, learning progress, compliance evidence, and career signals can travel responsibly across departments. The goal is not surveillance; it is continuity. A student should not become invisible because one department's sheet was not shared with another. A parent should not receive five conflicting messages. A principal should not wait weeks for a report that already exists in fragments across the institution.
The Rise of Unified Platforms

Globally, platforms such as Canvas and Blackboard helped normalize the idea that learning needs a digital environment. Enterprise ERPs normalized structured administration. Communication tools normalized real-time coordination. The next stage combines these previously separate categories into a unified campus platform: ERP for administration, LMS for learning, communication for engagement, analytics for decision-making, compliance for accountability, and AI for guided support.

body.caption: A unified platform connects departments as one operating layer rather than a chain of disconnected tools.

children.text: India needs this model, but it cannot simply import it. Indian institutions face high student volumes, fee workflows that must fit local payment habits, attendance and compliance rules that vary by board or regulator, a strong mobile-first student base, and operating teams that cannot spend years on implementation. The winning model will be practical, local, and institution-aware. It will reduce administrative load while helping students move from admission to learning, assessment, mentoring, and placement readiness with fewer invisible gaps.
Where Classgrid Fits

Classgrid's relevance comes from the fact that it was built from firsthand institutional pain points, not from a distant software brief. The student team behind the platform, including Nikhil Shinde, Swaroop Ghorpade, Krushna Gore, and other contributors, experienced the friction of disconnected campus systems directly. They did not begin with a narrow module thesis; they began with the daily reality of students, faculty, departments, and administrators trying to coordinate college life through fragmented tools.

That origin matters. A unified education platform for India must understand admissions, fees, attendance, classroom collaboration, assessments, communication, reports, compliance, AI assistance, mobile notifications, and institutional analytics as parts of one operating model. It must be powerful enough for administrators, simple enough for faculty, visible enough for students, and flexible enough for schools, colleges, engineering institutions, coaching centres, and junior colleges. Classgrid's mission is therefore not to add another dashboard to an already crowded ecosystem. It is to help institutions replace operational fragmentation with a coherent digital foundation.
What the 2030 Campus Operating Model Looks Like

The 2030-ready institution will treat every major workflow as part of one student journey. Admission will not end when a form is submitted; it will become the first record in a living academic profile. Attendance will not be an isolated compliance ritual; it will become an early-warning signal. Fees will not be a separate ledger; they will connect to communication, student services, and institutional planning. Learning will not stop inside the LMS; it will connect to assessment, mentoring, project evidence, and placement readiness. Communication will not disappear into private chats; it will become accountable, searchable, and role-aware.

children.text: Closing Perspective

The future of education technology in India is not a question of whether institutions will digitize. They already are. The real question is whether digitization will remain fragmented or become institutional infrastructure. The evidence is clear: scale is rising, employability expectations are changing, AI is rewriting workplace readiness, and national policy is pushing toward interoperable digital capacity. Institutions that unify ERP, LMS, communication, analytics, and student-readiness workflows will be better positioned to serve students with speed, clarity, and accountability.

conclusion: The future of education technology in India is not a question of whether institutions will digitize; it is whether digitization will become unified infrastructure. Classgrid is positioned for that shift because it was born from the lived operating pain of Indian institutions and built to connect the workflows that shape student outcomes.
